summary: Postgraduate scholarships at the University of Cambridge for citizens of any country outside the United Kingdom. Eligible courses: full-time or part-time PhD (part-time funding is being piloted), the full-time MLitt, and full-time one-year postgraduate courses with some exceptions. Current Cambridge students may apply for a new postgraduate course (for example a PhD after an MPhil) but not to fund the rest of a course already started. Not considered: undergraduate degrees, MASt courses, part-time degrees other than the PhD, and professional or non-standard degrees such as MBA, EMBA, MFin, PGCE and MD. Selection: Round 1 is for US citizens resident in the USA, and Round 2, the larger round, is for all other eligible applicants, including US citizens living, studying or working overseas. Applications opened 11 September 2026.
route_name: Online application via the University of Cambridge and Gates Cambridge
deadline_source_text: Round 1 (US citizens resident in the USA): deadline 11:59pm UK time on Wednesday 14 October 2026 (closed). Outcomes: Round 1 by 14 December 2026, Round 2 by 8 March 2027.

summary: Scholarships to encourage international exchange and research cooperation, open to applicants from 183 eligible countries with a maximum age of 35. Research scholarships are mainly for early-career researchers who have completed a master's degree and who have a supervisor at a Swiss cantonal university, university of applied sciences, ETH Zurich, EPFL or one of four ETH Domain research institutes. Art scholarships are for students starting an initial master's in an artistic field and are available only to a limited number of countries. Applications go to Swiss diplomatic representations abroad and are free; the commission warns about fake offers that ask for money. Award decisions for the following academic year are announced by the end of May at the latest, and 2028-29 scholarships are advertised from August 2027.
